previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 30-year-old woman with Type 1 diabetes and gastroparesis was admitted for recurrent intractable nausea and vomiting, unable to tolerate oral intake. She was managed with NPO status, IV fluids, and antiemetics including ondansetron, prochlorperazine, and lorazepam. Her blood glucose was elevated with ketonuria, prompting an increase in her Lantus dose from 28 to 31 units and adjustment of her sliding scale insulin. Hypertension, likely exacerbated by acute illness, was treated with IV hydralazine and transitioned to oral lisinopril 20 mg daily and metoprolol 50 mg twice daily. A CT head with contrast showed no central cause for her symptoms. Her nausea resolved, diet was advanced successfully, and she remained stable. She was discharged home with medication changes and instructions to follow up with her primary care provider and endocrinologist.
problems: Diabetes with neurological manifestations, type I [juvenile type], uncontrolled

Brief Hospital Course:
___ with h/o DM c/b gastroparesis presents with n/v.  
.  
# N/V. Seems most consistent with past episodes of 
gastroparesis. Comforting that recent gastric emptying study 
normal. No evidence of SBO (passing stool and flatus). No CP or 
other symptoms to suggest ACS. No UTI. Treated with IVF, NPO 
then advanced diet slowly as tolerated, standing reglan, PRN 
ativan/compazine/zofran, bid PPI. Patient's nausea resolved, 
without abdominal pain, able to tolerate PO. On discharge, felt 
back to her baseline.
.  
# Tachycardia. Patient with n/v/poor PO intake, likely resulting 
in dehydration and secondary tachycardia. No acute changes on 
EKG. No CP, SOB. Resolved with IVF hydration.
.  
# DM. Hyperglycemic on admission, perhaps low-grade DKA was 
present, improved on the floor. Used glargine and HISS, 
resolved.
.  
# HTN. High in ED in setting of vomiting/retching. Treated with 
IV lopressor; improved; changed back to home PO metoprolol for 
discharge.
